entities.summary:
Nanker was a Polish nobleman of Oksza coat of arms who played a significant role in the religious and political landscape of 14th-century Eastern Europe.

As bishop of Kraków (1320–1326) and bishop of Wrocław (1326–1341), Nanker worked to consolidate power and influence in the region, often in collaboration with the Polish king, Louis IV.

Despite his efforts, Nanker's legacy was not without controversy, as he faced opposition from local clergy and nobles who sought to limit his authority.

In his later years, Nanker became increasingly associated with the Franciscan Order, which would go on to shape the spiritual landscape of Eastern Europe for centuries to come.

As a testament to his enduring influence, Nanker's name remains a reminder of the complex web of power and faith that defined the medieval world.

The Kraków Cathedral, built during Nanker's tenure as bishop, stands as a testament to the enduring legacy of this enigmatic figure.

Nanker's story is one of intrigue, power, and spirituality, a fascinating chapter in the complex narrative of Eastern European history.
